licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages in two chunks, each by two independent readers, with a judge settling every difference and a sweep for the marks, then a fresh check by two proofreaders until clean; every bar of every part adds up. The Italian translation, the notes printed only for it, and the stage directions are left out. Allegro, 6/8, G major, from a two-eighth upbeat; Andante from bar 122; Allegretto, alla breve, C major, from bar 132 (the three Boys); Allegro, alla breve, from bar 165 (the glockenspiel). Papageno's panpipe is in the piano part as a third right-hand voice at sounding pitch, where his own line rests; the spoken “Eins, zwei, drei” have no notes. The glockenspiel is in the piano part as printed, its 8va written out. Each Boy has his own line; the print puts the First and Second Boys on one staff in places, and a note printed once for two Boys is sung by both. Playback tempo from complete recordings: the median length of this scene, 5:22, from Klemperer 1964 (5:36), Nézet-Séguin 2018 (5:24), Toscanini 1937 (5:22), Christie 1995 (5:12) and Solti 1969 (5:10); no recording splits it, so the four tempos keep an assumed proportion (the Andante's beat half the Allegro's; the Allegretto's half note the Allegro's dotted quarter; the closing Allegro a fifth faster than the Allegretto), with the fermatas held.
